bio_en: German Baroque composer and organist. Known as the "Father of Music", he is counted among the greatest composers in Western music history. He came from the Bach family, which produced more than fifty musicians over two hundred years, and served as cantor (music director) of St. Thomas Church in Leipzig, where he composed a great many sacred works and instrumental pieces.
style_en: pinnacle of counterpoint, perfection of the fugue, summation of Baroque style, fusion of German, Italian and French styles, intricate and complex harmony, deep religiosity, ornamented melodic lines
influence_en: Bach brought the music of the Baroque together and took it to its peak. He absorbed every genre and technique of his day and raised them to a perfect form. His harmony and counterpoint in particular became the foundation of Western music theory. In the Classical era after his death, his music was treated as old-fashioned and briefly forgotten. In the 19th century, however, Mendelssohn's revival of the St Matthew Passion set off a "Bach revival". Since then he has exerted an enormous influence, as a "textbook of music", on nearly every later composer, including Mozart, Beethoven and Chopin. To this day he is called the "Father of Music" and revered as one of the greatest composers.

bio_en: Monteverdi was an Italian composer, viola da gamba player and conductor. A key figure who led the transition from the Renaissance to the Baroque, he is often called the "father of opera". At the court of Mantua he composed the early operatic masterpiece Orfeo; later, as maestro di cappella of St Mark's Basilica in Venice, he left grand sacred works such as the Vespers of the Blessed Virgin and late operatic masterpieces such as The Coronation of Poppea.
style_en: second practice (Seconda pratica), vehement expression of emotion (Stile concitato), dramatic use of dissonance, monody, differentiation of recitative and aria, text-centered composition
influence_en: Monteverdi advocated and established the "seconda pratica", which put the emotion and drama of the words ahead of the complex counterpoint rules of the earlier Renaissance style, known as the "prima pratica". This became the central aesthetic of the Baroque, in which music serves as a tool for portraying the emotion of the text. His opera Orfeo is regarded as the first great opera, not a mere court entertainment but a perfect union of drama and music, and it became the effective starting point of a genre that would continue for the next 300 years.

bio_en: Händel was a great Baroque composer who was born in Germany and spent most of his working life, until his death, in England. Together with J.S. Bach, born in the same year, he is called one of the two towering figures of the Baroque. After mastering opera in Italy, he settled in London, where he composed some forty Italian operas with great success. When English public taste later changed, he pioneered a new genre, the English-language "oratorio", and left immortal masterpieces such as Messiah. His music is marked by dramatic effect, grand scale, and clear, vigorous melodies.
style_en: dramatic intensity, grand choruses, clear homophonic harmony, Italian opera seria, English oratorio, brilliant orchestration, fluent and emotional melodic lines
influence_en: Händel was the effective founder of the English oratorio. He brought sacred dramatic music out of the church and into the theater, making it popular, and Messiah in particular had a profound influence on later composers up to Haydn, Mozart and Beethoven. His Italian operas dominated London's musical life of the day, and orchestral suites such as the Water Music and the Music for the Royal Fireworks set the model for outdoor and festival music.

bio_en: Antonio Vivaldi was an Italian composer of the Baroque and the finest violin virtuoso of his day. Because of his red hair he was nicknamed "Il Prete Rosso" (the Red Priest). He taught for many years at the Ospedale della Pietà, a Venetian orphanage and music school, and composed some 500 concertos for its outstanding all-female orchestra. His music is marked by lively rhythms, clear melodies and dramatic contrasts, and The Four Seasons in particular has transcended its era to remain one of the best-loved classical works today.
style_en: master of the concerto, establishment of ritornello form, lively rhythm, clear and bright melody, dramatic dynamic contrast (tutti vs. solo), virtuosic violin technique, program music
influence_en: Vivaldi established the solo concerto in three movements, fast–slow–fast, and perfected ritornello form (a form in which the main theme returns repeatedly). This became the standard for the Baroque concerto and carried through to the Classical concerto. His innovative style had a profound influence on J.S. Bach, who arranged many of Vivaldi's concertos for keyboard instruments and studied his style in the process. His music was forgotten for over a century after his death, but it was reappraised in the early 20th century when Bach's arrangements came to light, and he is now regarded as one of the most important composers of the Baroque.

bio_en: Henry Purcell is one of the greatest English Baroque composers. He showed such originality and talent that he was nicknamed "Orpheus Britannicus". Despite a short life, as organist of the Chapel Royal and royal composer he left masterpieces in every genre of his day: church music, stage music (semi-opera), instrumental music and songs. Dido and Aeneas, his only true opera, is considered the finest work in the history of English opera.
style_en: distinctly English lyricism, combination of Italian and French styles, bold use of dissonance, ground bass (a repeating bass line), expressive word painting, semi-opera
influence_en: Purcell perfected a distinctive English Baroque style by combining Italian and French musical styles with English sensibility and originality. His music marked the peak of English music until Händel came to England. Dido and Aeneas in particular is regarded as the origin and greatest masterpiece of English opera, and pieces such as "Dido's Lament" show tragic expression at its height through the ground bass technique. After his death English music came under Händel's influence, but Purcell's originality was rediscovered and became a great inspiration to later English composers of the 20th century such as Benjamin Britten.

bio_en: Domenico Scarlatti was an Italian composer and a master of the harpsichord (cembalo). He was born the son of the famous opera composer Alessandro Scarlatti, and by coincidence in exactly the same year as J.S. Bach and Händel (1685). He spent most of his career at the courts of Portugal and Spain, where he composed some 555 keyboard sonatas for the Spanish princess (later queen) María Bárbara. His sonatas break away from the contrapuntal style of the Baroque and are original works marked by bold harmony, innovative technique and strong touches of Spanish folk music.
style_en: 555 keyboard sonatas, single movements (binary form), harpsichord virtuosity, bold harmony, cross-hand technique, influence of Spanish folk rhythms and guitar techniques, rapid scales and arpeggios, acciaccatura (a short grace note creating a dissonance)
influence_en: Scarlatti greatly expanded the limits of harpsichord (and early piano) technique. Stylistically his sonatas are closer to the clear homophony (harmonic music) of the Classical era than to the complex counterpoint of the Baroque. His bold harmonic progressions, hand-crossing, wide leaps and rapid repeated notes in particular had a huge impact on later keyboard music, inspiring Chopin and Liszt of the Romantic era by way of Muzio Clementi. His sonatas are now a core part of pianists' repertoire.

bio_en: Jean-Philippe Rameau was the most important French Baroque composer and a great music theorist called the "father of modern harmony". After the death of Jean-Baptiste Lully, he reigned as the foremost master of French opera. At the late age of fifty he stunned the Parisian musical world with his debut opera, Hippolyte et Aricie; until then he had worked mainly as an organist and composer of harpsichord (clavecin) music. His music is characterized by rich and bold harmony, dramatic expressiveness and innovative orchestration.
style_en: rich and bold harmony, innovative orchestration, establishment of functional harmony, dramatic recitative, French opera (tragédie lyrique, opéra-ballet), clavecin (harpsichord) suites, descriptive character pieces, Rococo elegance
influence_en: Rameau's influence is immense in both composition and theory. His 1722 treatise Traité de l'harmonie earned him the title "father of modern harmony". In it he was the first to systematize the concept of chord inversion and the functional roles of the primary triads (tonic, dominant, subdominant), establishing the foundation of all later Western music theory. As a composer, he carried on the French opera established by Lully and added rich harmony and dramatic orchestration, realizing "drama through music". His arrival was so innovative that it provoked a fierce musical quarrel between the Lullistes (traditionalists) and the Ramistes (innovators).

bio_en: Telemann was a leading German Baroque composer and one of the most prolific composers in history. He was a close friend of J.S. Bach (and godfather to Bach's son C.P.E. Bach), and in his lifetime he enjoyed a reputation greater than that of Bach or Händel. He turned down the post of cantor at St. Thomas Church in Leipzig (which Bach later took), working instead as music director in Hamburg, where he composed more than 3,000 works of church and instrumental music. His music is regarded as the essence of the "mixed style", a perfect blend of German rigor, French elegance and Italian vitality.
style_en: astonishing productivity (more than 3,000 works, TWV), German-French-Italian "mixed style", forerunner of the galant style (Stile Galante), elegant and refined melodies, attempts at program music, Tafelmusik (table music), music publishing and dissemination
influence_en: Telemann was a key figure in popularizing the galant style, which bridges the late Baroque and early Classical. His music strongly influenced his contemporaries, and his work in Hamburg in particular contributed greatly to the development of the public concert. He was also active in music publishing, distributing many scores that amateur musicians could easily approach and so helping to make music more popular.

bio_en: Arcangelo Corelli was a leading Italian Baroque composer and the finest violin virtuoso of his day. Based mainly in Rome, he laid the foundations of modern violin technique and is called the "father of modern violin playing". His output is small in quantity (six published collections in all), but its near-perfect formal beauty, elegance and clarity had an enormous influence across Europe at the time.
style_en: perfection of the concerto grosso style, master of the trio sonata, clear and balanced form, lyrical melodic lines, "singing" violin lines, rational harmonic progressions
influence_en: Corelli perfected two central Baroque instrumental forms, the concerto grosso (ensemble concerto) and the trio sonata (sonata for three instruments). His Op. 6 concerti grossi were a direct model for the concertos of later composers such as Vivaldi, Händel and Bach. He also systematized and taught violin fingering and bowing, and through his many pupils formed the "Corelli school", spreading violin technique across Europe.

bio_en: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, born in Salzburg, Austria, is one of the greatest composers of the Classical era. Known as a child prodigy, he began composing at the age of five and, together with his father Leopold, toured Europe from an early age, winning fame. Despite a short life of thirty-five years, he left more than 600 immortal masterpieces in every genre of his day: symphonies, operas, concertos, chamber music and sacred music.
style_en: perfect balance and formal beauty, genius for melody, clear and transparent harmony, dramatic operatic writing (a masterly union of recitative and aria), perfection of the piano concerto, harmony of elegance (galant style) and dramatic expression
influence_en: Together with Haydn, Mozart established the "First Viennese School" and brought it to its peak. He took over the forms of symphony and string quartet that Haydn had established and filled them with richer and more dramatic content. The piano concerto style he perfected, and his innovative operatic writing in works such as The Marriage of Figaro, Don Giovanni and The Magic Flute, had a profound influence on Beethoven and later Romantic composers. His music is today a byword for "perfect beauty".

bio_en: Ludwig van Beethoven was a composer born in Bonn, Germany, who worked in Vienna, Austria. Called the "Sage of Music", he brought the Classical era to completion and opened the door to the Romantic. Building on the Classical forms established by Haydn and Mozart, he infused his music with intense emotions such as personal anguish, struggle and joy. Even in the face of the devastating ordeal of losing his hearing, he composed some of the greatest masterpieces in human history, including the Eroica, the Fifth and the Ninth (Choral) symphonies.
style_en: intense dynamic contrasts, vast forms and scale, relentless development of motifs, drama of struggle and triumph, combination of Classical formal beauty and Romantic content, profound inwardness and contrapuntal complexity in the late works
influence_en: Beethoven raised the status of the musician from a mere craftsman to a "tormented artist". He stretched Classical sonata form to its limit and lifted the symphony into a genre that carries humanitarian and philosophical messages. His nine symphonies stood like a great mountain range over every later Romantic composer (Brahms, Wagner, Mahler and others), and his music came to symbolize the very spirit of the age, "liberty, equality, fraternity".

bio_en: Franz Joseph Haydn was an Austrian composer called the "father of the symphony" and the "father of the string quartet". For many years he served as Kapellmeister at the court of the Esterházy family, where the stable environment let him experiment and create again and again. Through more than 100 symphonies and more than 60 string quartets he established the foundations of Classical instrumental style. His humorous, cheerful character is well reflected in his music; he shared a deep friendship with Mozart and also taught Beethoven.
style_en: establishment of the symphony and string quartet forms, perfection of sonata form, clear formal beauty, wit and humor (e.g. the Surprise Symphony), use of folk melodies, inventive development of themes, stable and balanced orchestration
influence_en: Without Haydn, there would have been no music of Mozart or Beethoven. He set the standard for the four-movement symphony and raised the string quartet to a serious chamber-music genre in which four instruments converse as equals. His music became the model of Classical style itself, and his late oratorios, The Creation and The Seasons in particular, carried on Händel's tradition and influenced Romantic choral music.

bio_en: Antonio Salieri was an Italian-born composer, conductor and teacher who worked in Vienna, Austria. In his day, as Hofkapellmeister of the Viennese court, succeeding Gluck, he enjoyed the highest renown as an opera composer. He is portrayed as Mozart's rival in the film Amadeus, but in reality he was a great teacher who taught many geniuses, including Beethoven, Schubert, Liszt and Czerny.
style_en: master of Italian opera seria and opera buffa, continuation of Gluck's spirit of operatic reform, clear and dramatic vocal melodies, fluent orchestration, stable formal beauty
influence_en: As a composer he achieved great success in his day but was overshadowed by Mozart and Beethoven. His greatest historical influence, however, was as a teacher. He taught vocal composition to Beethoven and composition to Schubert and Liszt, training many pupils who bridged the Classical and Romantic eras and serving as a godfather figure of Viennese musical life.

bio_en: Carl Czerny was an Austrian pianist, composer and one of the most important piano teachers in history. He was a pupil of Beethoven and studied composition with Antonio Salieri. He also left many works as a composer, including symphonies and concertos, but today his name has won immortal fame through thousands of piano études (studies), such as the Czerny 30, 40 and 50 collections. He was also Franz Liszt's only formal teacher.
style_en: systematic piano technique études, Classical clarity, technical training in scales, arpeggios and the like, works for teaching
influence_en: Czerny's études made a decisive contribution to the development of 19th-century piano technique. Through his pupil Franz Liszt, his systematic teaching method opened the age of "virtuoso" pianism, and it is still used as a basic textbook by piano students around the world today.

bio_en: Leopold Mozart was a German-born composer, violinist and music theorist. He was deputy Kapellmeister at the Salzburg court, and above all he is best known as the father and teacher of Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart. He recognized his son's genius early and devoted his life to presenting him across Europe. He was himself a fine composer, and his Toy Symphony in particular is famous.
style_en: early Classical (galant style), clear and easy-listening melodies, violin technique, witty descriptive music (e.g. the Toy Symphony)
influence_en: His greatest influence was in educating his son Wolfgang. His treatise A Treatise on the Fundamental Principles of Violin Playing, published in 1756, was one of the most important textbooks of violin technique in its day and remains an essential source for studying 18th-century performance practice.

bio_en: Luigi Boccherini was an Italian-born cellist and composer who worked mainly in Spain. A contemporary of Haydn, he composed a great many works of chamber music and is especially known for raising the cello's standing as a solo instrument. His music has an elegant, sentimental Italian and Spanish coloring, different from Haydn's Viennese Classical style. Boccherini's Minuet (the third movement of the String Quintet Op. 11, No. 5) is famous worldwide.
style_en: cello virtuoso, elegant and lyrical melodies (galant style), pioneer of the string quintet style (with two cellos), Spanish-flavored rhythms and coloring
influence_en: Boccherini dramatically advanced the cello repertoire through his cello concertos and chamber music with cello. Just as Haydn perfected the string quartet, he pioneered and perfected the distinctive genre of the string quintet with two cellos.

bio_en: Christoph Willibald Gluck was a German-born composer who led the "opera reform" of the late 18th century. He criticized the Italian opera of his day for focusing only on singers' displays of virtuosity (coloratura) and losing the essence of drama. Working mainly in Vienna and Paris, under the banner that "music must serve drama and poetry", he composed solemn and noble operas that dispensed with unnecessary ornament and stayed true to the content of the drama. His best-known work is Orfeo ed Euridice.
style_en: "noble simplicity", drama-centered opera, breaking down the boundary between recitative and aria, active use of chorus and ballet, pursuit of dramatic truth
influence_en: Gluck's opera reform changed the course of operatic history. His ideals directly influenced Mozart's Idomeneo and Don Giovanni, among others, and he went on to serve as a forerunner of the "music drama" (Musikdrama) ideal of Weber and Wagner. He was a great innovator who raised the question of the relationship between music and drama in the history of music.

bio_en: Carl Philipp Emanuel Bach was the second son of J.S. Bach, known as the "Berlin Bach" or the "Hamburg Bach". He was the most important and original composer of the transitional period between his father's Baroque style and the Classical style of Haydn and Mozart. He served at the court of Frederick the Great of Prussia and later as music director in Hamburg. His music represents the "Empfindsamer Stil" (sensitive style), which valued the intense expression of subjective emotion.
style_en: Empfindsamer Stil (sensitive style), abrupt changes of mood and dynamics, unexpected harmonic progressions and modulations, expressive keyboard music for clavichord and harpsichord (early piano)
influence_en: C.P.E. Bach had a direct and profound influence on Haydn, Mozart and Beethoven. (Haydn: "I owe everything to him.") His treatise Essay on the True Art of Playing Keyboard Instruments was the finest instruction book of its day, and his sonatas and symphonies made a decisive contribution to the development of Classical sonata form. He was a key figure who served as a bridge from the Baroque to the Classical.

bio_en: Johann Christian Bach was the youngest son of J.S. Bach, known as the "London Bach". After studying opera in Italy, he settled in London, where he achieved great success. In complete contrast to his father's complex counterpoint, he was a master of the "galant style" (Stile Galante), marked by graceful, song-like melodies. He made a great impression on the eight-year-old Mozart, who visited London in 1764, and also performed with him.
style_en: galant style (Stile Galante), graceful, singing cantabile melodies, clear and simple harmony, early Classical symphony, Italian operatic style, use of the Alberti bass in concertos
influence_en: J.C. Bach taught the young Mozart how to compose "concerto form" and "singing allegro" movements. His influence was decisive for the formation of Mozart's early style, to the point that Mozart said he had "learned everything from him". He made an important contribution to the development of the Classical concerto and symphony.

bio_en: Johann Stamitz was a Czech-born composer and violinist, the founder of the German "Mannheim School". He trained the Mannheim court orchestra to the finest level in Europe at the time, and made a great contribution there to the development of the symphony. He helped establish the standard form of the symphony by introducing the four-movement structure and adding a minuet as the third movement.
style_en: Mannheim School, introduction of the four-movement symphony form, the "Mannheim crescendo" (a technique in which the whole orchestra gradually grows louder), the "Mannheim rocket" (a rising arpeggio theme), precise orchestral ensemble and dynamic expression
influence_en: The innovative orchestral techniques and symphonic form of Stamitz and the Mannheim School directly influenced Haydn and Mozart. The introduction of dynamic effects such as the "crescendo" in particular played a decisive role in developing the symphony into a dramatic genre. He was a pioneer who laid the foundations of the symphony before Haydn, the "father of the symphony".

bio_en: Muzio Clementi was an Italian-born composer, pianist, piano maker and publisher. Called the "father of the pianoforte", he is famous for an anecdote of a piano contest with Mozart in Vienna in 1781. Based mainly in London, he explored the possibilities of the new instrument, the piano, to the fullest. His collection of studies Gradus ad Parnassum laid the foundations of modern piano technique.
style_en: modern piano technique (scales, progressions in thirds and sixths, octaves), sonatinas, Classical sonata form, brilliant virtuosity, legato playing
influence_en: Clementi established a brilliant, virtuosic playing style, unlike Mozart's, that exploited the mechanical properties of the piano. This directly influenced Beethoven (who thought highly of Clementi's sonatas), and his collection of studies served as a bridge, by way of Czerny, to the Romantic pianism of Chopin and Liszt.

bio_en: Austrian composer. He revered Beethoven and, by infusing the Classical framework with Romantic lyricism, came to be called the "king of the Lied". In a short life of thirty-one years he left many masterpieces, including some 600 songs as well as symphonies and chamber music. His music served as a perfect bridge from the Classical to the Romantic.
style_en: king of the Lied (art song), perfect union of poetry and music, rich and lyrical melodies, bold harmony and modulation, the "wanderer" theme, the Unfinished Symphony
influence_en: He raised the German art song (Lied) into an independent art form. His song cycles, including Die schöne Müllerin and Winterreise, had a profound influence on later composers such as Schumann, Brahms and Wolf. The Symphony No. 9, the "Great", was unearthed by Schumann and is regarded as a masterpiece of the Romantic symphony.

bio_en: German composer, conductor and pianist. A genius raised in comfortable circumstances, he is called a "classical Romantic" for combining Classical balance with Romantic lyricism. He is famous for the Violin Concerto in E minor and the overture to A Midsummer Night's Dream, and he was also the man who set off the "Bach revival" by reviving Bach's forgotten St Matthew Passion.
style_en: Classical formal beauty, graceful and refined melodies, light and fantastical scherzos, descriptive program music (e.g. Fingal's Cave)
influence_en: His Violin Concerto in E minor, together with the concertos of Brahms and Tchaikovsky, is counted among the three great Romantic violin concertos. By reviving the forgotten music of Bach he also had an enormous influence on 19th-century music history, and as conductor of the Leipzig Gewandhaus Orchestra he laid the foundations of modern conducting.

bio_en: Composer and pianist of Polish origin. Called the "poet of the piano", he devoted most of his life to composing solo piano music. He left his homeland Poland and worked in Paris, elevating Polish folk rhythms (the mazurka and the polonaise) into art music.
style_en: solo piano music (nocturnes, ballades, études, waltzes and more), Polish folk rhythms (mazurka, polonaise), delicate and lyrical melodies, original harmony, rubato, poetic sensibility
influence_en: Chopin pushed the expressive power of the piano to its limit. His innovative technique, harmony and pedalling had an absolute influence on all later composers for the piano, including Liszt, Debussy and Rachmaninoff. In the history of piano music he stands shoulder to shoulder with Bach, Mozart and Beethoven.

bio_en: A composer who was the very embodiment of the German Romantic spirit. Deeply versed in literature, he left many lyrical short piano pieces and songs that combine music and literature. He is also famous for his love story with his wife, Clara Schumann, and, working as a critic as well, he discovered new talents such as Chopin and Brahms.
style_en: literary sensibility, character pieces (short piano works), song cycles (Liederkreis), contrast of passion (Florestan) and reverie (Eusebius), cross-rhythm, poetic titles
influence_en: In piano suites and song cycles Schumann, following Schubert, left unrivaled achievements. His music criticism (in the Neue Zeitschrift für Musik) led opinion in the 19th-century musical world, and his discovery of Brahms in particular, naming him as his heir, had a great effect on music history.

bio_en: Hungarian-born composer and one of the greatest pianists in history. Impressed by hearing Paganini play, he resolved to become the "Paganini of the piano", and with superhuman technique and charisma he gave rise to the new word "Lisztomania". In his later years he devoted himself to composition and created a new genre, the "symphonic poem".
style_en: transcendent virtuosity, invention of the piano recital, invention of the symphonic poem, thematic transformation technique, Hungarian folk music elements
influence_en: Liszt laid the foundations of modern piano technique, and his "symphonic poems", together with Wagner's music dramas, became the peak of Romantic program music. He was also a steadfast supporter of Wagner and greatly influenced nationalist composers such as Smetana and Grieg.

bio_en: German composer, conductor and theorist. He was the founder of the "music drama" (Musikdrama) that changed the history of opera. He sought to elevate traditional opera into the "total work of art" (Gesamtkunstwerk), and founded the Bayreuth Festival Theatre himself to stage the four-part Ring of the Nibelung.
style_en: music drama (Musikdrama), total work of art (Gesamtkunstwerk), leitmotif, endless melody, chromatic harmony (the Tristan chord), enormous orchestral forces
influence_en: Wagner is among the most influential composers in the history of Western music. His innovative harmony (the Tristan chord) opened the door to 20th-century atonal music, and his music-drama ideals and orchestration had an enormous influence on later composers such as Richard Strauss, Mahler, Debussy and Schoenberg.

bio_en: The "king of opera", representing 19th-century Italian opera. He is often compared with Wagner, his rival born in the same year. He was a symbolic figure of the Italian unification movement (the Risorgimento), and left many operatic masterpieces that portray human emotion dramatically, such as Rigoletto, La traviata and Aida.
style_en: peak of Italian opera, dramatic expression through the human voice, melody-centered writing (bel canto), intense drama, organic combination of recitative and aria, late works Otello and Falstaff
influence_en: Verdi inherited and perfected the tradition of Italian opera. His operas are among the best-loved repertoire in opera houses around the world today, and they directly influenced later composers of "verismo" (realist) opera, including Puccini.

bio_en: German composer. Named by Schumann as "Beethoven's heir", he stood against the Wagner-Liszt "New German School" to become a master of "neoclassicism", carrying on the Beethoven tradition. A perfectionist, he took more than twenty years to complete his First Symphony. In the Romantic era he showed the essence of Classical formal beauty.
style_en: neoclassicism, absolute music, four symphonies, A German Requiem, revival of counterpoint and Classical formal beauty, Romantic lyricism, cross-rhythm, rich and dark harmony
influence_en: In the Romantic era Brahms did not get swept along by the current of program music, and reasserted the value of "absolute music" in the symphony and chamber music. His four symphonies, together with Beethoven's nine, became standard symphonic repertoire, and his music also had a great influence on 20th-century composers such as Schoenberg.

bio_en: The greatest composer of Russian Romanticism. He composed the three great ballet scores, Swan Lake, The Nutcracker and The Sleeping Beauty, and expressed Russian sorrow and lyricism superbly in works such as the Symphony No. 6, the "Pathétique". Unlike the Russian nationalist school, he actively embraced Western European musical styles.
style_en: Russian Romanticism, brilliant orchestration, tragic and plaintive melodies, elevation of ballet music to symphonic level, Piano Concerto No. 1, Violin Concerto
influence_en: Tchaikovsky raised ballet music from mere accompaniment to an art on a par with the symphony. His music, which put Russian feeling into Western European forms, won universal sympathy and had a profound influence on later Russian composers such as Rachmaninoff and Shostakovich.

bio_en: Italian violinist and composer. With superhuman technique and charisma that earned him the name "the devil's violinist", he swept across Europe. His playing inspired Liszt and opened the Romantic age of the "virtuoso".
style_en: transcendent virtuosity (double stops, flageolet harmonics, left-hand pizzicato), 24 Caprices, violin concertos, brilliant variations
influence_en: Paganini stretched the limits of violin technique to the extreme. His 24 Caprices have been used again and again as variation themes by later composers (Liszt, Brahms, Rachmaninoff), exerting an enormous influence.

bio_en: The foremost master of Italian opera in the first half of the 19th century. He had unrivaled success especially in opera buffa (comic opera), with works such as The Barber of Seville and Cinderella (La cenerentola). He is famous for the anecdote that after William Tell he suddenly retired at the age of 37 and spent the rest of his life as a gourmet.
style_en: opera buffa, bel canto singing, the "Rossini crescendo" (gradual build-up), brilliant vocal virtuosity, lively rhythm
influence_en: Rossini perfected the genre of opera buffa, and his melodic writing and orchestration laid the foundations of Italian opera that led through Bellini and Donizetti to Verdi.

bio_en: An innovative composer representing French Romanticism. In the Symphonie fantastique he used the "idée fixe" technique to express his own experience through program music. He was a master of orchestration, and his treatise on orchestration is still used as a textbook today.
style_en: program music, idée fixe, innovative orchestration, vast forces (e.g. the Requiem), literary inspiration (Shakespeare, Goethe)
influence_en: Berlioz dramatically expanded the possibilities of the symphony, and his ideas about program music and his orchestration directly influenced Liszt (the symphonic poem), Wagner (music drama) and Richard Strauss.

bio_en: The "father of the Russian nationalist school". He was the first composer to combine Russian folk music and language with Western European operatic and symphonic technique. His operas A Life for the Tsar and Ruslan and Lyudmila opened a distinctly Russian operatic tradition.
style_en: founder of the Russian nationalist school, use of Russian folk melodies and rhythms, opera, the orchestral work Kamarinskaya
influence_en: Glinka's music had an absolute influence on the Russian "Five" (Balakirev, Mussorgsky, Rimsky-Korsakov and others), and became the foundation for all later Russian composers, including Tchaikovsky.

bio_en: The finest female pianist and a composer of the 19th century. She was the wife of Robert Schumann and a lifelong friend of Johannes Brahms. In the male-dominated musical world of her day she was recognized as a leading virtuoso, and she devoted herself to premiering her husband's works and bringing them to a wide audience.
style_en: Romantic pianism, piano concerto, piano trio, lyrical short piano pieces, songs
influence_en: As a performer, Clara Schumann played a decisive role in interpreting and spreading the works of Chopin, Schumann and Brahms. Her presence and works also proved the possibilities open to women musicians in the 19th century and greatly inspired later women composers.

bio_en: French composer and organist born in Belgium. As a professor at the Paris Conservatoire he formed the "Franck school" and led the revival of French instrumental music in the late 19th century. Called the "father of the French symphony", he is famous for his Symphony in D minor and Violin Sonata in A major.
style_en: cyclic form, rich chromatic harmony, grand organ-like sonority, late Romanticism, French symphony, chamber music
influence_en: His pupils (d'Indy, Chausson and others) developed a distinctly French instrumental music centered on the Société Nationale de Musique, which became the foundation of French modern music leading to Fauré and Debussy.

bio_en: Austrian composer and organist. Grounded in devout Catholic faith, he composed nine grand, monumental symphonies. He deeply revered Wagner and was called the "Wagner of the symphony".
style_en: late Romantic symphony, vast scale, the "Bruckner organ" (organ-like orchestral sound), religious mysticism, influence of Wagner's harmony and orchestration
influence_en: Bruckner's symphonies, inheriting the tradition of Beethoven and Wagner, created a sublime and religious kind of symphonic music. His music built a direct bridge to the symphonies of Gustav Mahler.

bio_en: Austrian composer. Called the "Waltz King", he composed hundreds of waltzes and polkas, including The Blue Danube and Tales from the Vienna Woods, raising the Viennese waltz to the level of art. His operetta Die Fledermaus was also a great success.
style_en: perfection of the Viennese waltz, operetta, light and graceful melodies, polkas, marches, the "Waltz King"
influence_en: He elevated the waltz from a mere dance tune to a symphonic miniature that could be appreciated in the concert hall. Serious composers of his day, such as Brahms, Mahler and Richard Strauss, also thought highly of his music and were influenced by it.

bio_en: A member of the Russian "Five", he was the most original and radical composer of the group. He sought to express the feeling, language and rhythm unique to Russia in their raw form. His best-known works are Pictures at an Exhibition, the opera Boris Godunov and Night on Bald Mountain.
style_en: the Russian Five, nationalist school, intense realism, melodies that follow the inflections of the Russian language, unconventional harmony, shifting meters
influence_en: Mussorgsky's primitive, daring music was judged rough in his day but became widely known through Rimsky-Korsakov's arrangements. His originality was a tremendous inspiration to 20th-century composers such as Debussy, Ravel and Stravinsky.

bio_en: French composer. Though also known for works such as the L'Arlésienne suites, he won immortal fame with a single work, the opera Carmen. At its premiere Carmen was condemned for its shocking content, but just after Bizet's death it became a sensation across Europe.
style_en: the opera Carmen, exotic atmosphere (Spain), realistic subject matter, enchanting melodies, brilliant orchestration
influence_en: Carmen broke the tradition of French opera and directly influenced the birth of Italian "verismo" (realist) opera. Many of his contemporaries, including Brahms, Tchaikovsky and Nietzsche, praised Carmen highly.

bio_en: A leading composer of the Czech nationalist school. Following Smetana, he successfully combined Czech folk music with Classical forms such as the symphony and chamber music. While serving as director of the National Conservatory of Music in New York, he composed immortal masterpieces including the Symphony No. 9, "From the New World", and the Cello Concerto in B minor.
style_en: Czech nationalist school, Bohemian folk rhythms and melodies, Slavonic Dances, influence of Brahms (Classical formal beauty), rich orchestration
influence_en: His symphony From the New World gave the American musical world the message to "use their own folk music", and so influenced the development of American music. His Cello Concerto is regarded as the greatest of Romantic cello concertos.

bio_en: A member of the Russian "Five" and a composer called the "magician of orchestration". He is famous for exotic, vividly colored orchestral works such as Scheherazade and Capriccio espagnol. He also contributed greatly to arranging and completing the unfinished works of colleagues such as Mussorgsky.
style_en: magician of orchestration, brilliant and exotic colors, nationalist school of the Five, fairy-tale and fantastic subjects, Russian folk songs
influence_en: As professor at the St. Petersburg Conservatory he trained many younger composers, including Glazunov and Stravinsky. His Principles of Orchestration became a standard textbook, and his brilliant orchestration influenced Ravel, Respighi and others.

bio_en: French composer, organist and teacher. He was a key figure who served as a bridge from late Romanticism to 20th-century modern music. He is known for delicate, elegant music such as the Requiem, the Pavane and "After a Dream" (Après un rêve).
style_en: modern French song (mélodie), delicate and refined harmony, supple melodies, introverted lyricism, chamber music, the Requiem
influence_en: Fauré broke free of Wagner's influence and established a distinctly French musical idiom, delicate and restrained. His innovative harmonic progressions opened the way beyond Romanticism toward Impressionism, and his pupils (Ravel among them) became leading figures of 20th-century French music.

bio_en: The last great master of Italian opera, following Giuseppe Verdi. He composed some of the best-loved opera repertoire today, including La bohème, Tosca, Madama Butterfly and Turandot. Influenced by "verismo" (realist) opera, he portrayed the tragic love stories of ordinary people in moving melodies.
style_en: verismo opera, lyrical and emotional arias, dramatic orchestration, exotic subjects, intense drama
influence_en: Puccini was, in effect, the last figure to carry on Italian opera after Verdi. His operas capped Romantic opera and remain to this day the most important repertoire guaranteeing box-office success in opera houses around the world.

bio_en: Austrian composer and one of the finest conductors of his day. He made his name conducting at the Vienna State Opera and with the New York Philharmonic. As a composer he left huge, philosophical works, including nine symphonies and Das Lied von der Erde. His music announces the end of Romanticism and the beginning of 20th-century modernism.
style_en: peak of the late Romantic symphony, enormous forces, philosophical and pessimistic themes (death, resurrection, love), use of folk song (Lied) melodies, extreme emotional contrasts
influence_en: Mahler pushed the symphony to the limit of Romanticism. His music directly influenced the Second Viennese School (Schoenberg, Berg, Webern), leading to the birth of 20th-century atonal music and Expressionism.

bio_en: French composer and the founder of "Impressionist music". Like the Impressionist painters, he sought to express in music not clear outlines but momentary impressions, atmosphere and color. He is famous for Prélude à l'après-midi d'un faune and Clair de lune.
style_en: Impressionism, ambiguous tonality, use of whole-tone and pentatonic scales, parallel chords, focus on atmosphere and color
influence_en: Debussy moved away from the grandeur and exaggerated emotion of Romanticism, represented by Wagner, and opened a new door for 20th-century music. His innovative harmony and liberation of timbre had a profound influence on nearly every 20th-century composer, including Ravel, Stravinsky and Bartók.

bio_en: Russian composer, conductor and one of the greatest pianists of the 20th century. He is called the "last great master of Romanticism". After the Russian Revolution he emigrated to the United States. He is famous for virtuosic piano works such as the Piano Concertos No. 2 and No. 3 and the Rhapsody on a Theme of Paganini.
style_en: late Romanticism, piano technique for enormous hands, virtuosity, sweeping melodies tinged with sorrow, influence of Russian Orthodox church bells
influence_en: Amid the currents of 20th-century modernism, Rachmaninoff held fast to the Romantic idiom. His piano concertos, following Tchaikovsky's, capped the Romantic piano concerto and remain among the best-loved repertoire today.

bio_en: French composer who, with Debussy, represents Impressionist music. But he valued Classical formal beauty and clarity more than Debussy did. He was so gifted at orchestral arrangement that he was called the "magician of the orchestra", and he is famous for Boléro, Pavane for a Dead Princess, and his orchestration of Mussorgsky's Pictures at an Exhibition.
style_en: Impressionism, neoclassicism, refined orchestration, exotic (Spanish) atmosphere, jazz influence, Boléro
influence_en: Ravel led French music of the 20th century together with Debussy, and his refined music also influenced American composers such as Gershwin. His orchestration of Pictures at an Exhibition in particular became a textbook of orchestral arrangement, to the point that it is better known than the original piano work.

bio_en: German composer. With the opera Der Freischütz he opened a chapter of "German Romantic opera" based on German legends and folk songs.
style_en: founder of German Romantic opera, Der Freischütz, supernatural subjects, clarinet concertos
influence_en: His Der Freischütz directly influenced Richard Wagner and served as the bridge leading to the birth of the German "music drama".

bio_en: Austrian composer, called the "father of the waltz". He established the form of the Viennese waltz and made it fashionable across Europe. The Radetzky March remains an immortal work.
style_en: establishment of the Viennese waltz, the Radetzky March, polkas, marches
influence_en: He laid the foundation for developing the waltz from social dance music into concert music, a development completed by his son Johann Strauss II.

bio_en: French composer. He is best known as the composer of Giselle, one of the finest masterpieces of Romantic ballet. He also composed the Christmas carol "O Holy Night".
style_en: Romantic ballet Giselle, opéra comique, "O Holy Night"
influence_en: The ballet Giselle became the standard of Romantic ballet and remains one of the most important ballet repertoire pieces to this day.

bio_en: French composer. He had worldwide success with the opera Faust. He is also very famous for his Ave Maria, in which he set a melody over Prelude No. 1 from Book 1 of Bach's The Well-Tempered Clavier.
style_en: French lyric opera (drame lyrique), the opera Faust, the "Bach-Gounod Ave Maria"
influence_en: His opera Faust became the model of French opera in the late 19th century and influenced younger composers such as Jules Massenet.

bio_en: French composer born in Germany. Called the "king of operetta", he wrote many cheerful comic operas satirizing Parisian society of his day. He is famous for the "cancan" dance in Orpheus in the Underworld.
style_en: founder of operetta (comic opera), social satire, Orpheus in the Underworld (the cancan), The Tales of Hoffmann
influence_en: His operettas influenced Johann Strauss II (Vienna) and Gilbert and Sullivan (Britain), and so contributed to the later birth of the musical.

bio_en: The "father of the Czech nationalist school". Influenced by Liszt, he composed symphonic poems and operas based on Czech history, legend and nature. "Vltava" (The Moldau), the second piece of the symphonic poem cycle Má vlast (My Country), is world famous.
style_en: founder of the Czech nationalist school, the symphonic poem cycle Má vlast (Vltava), the opera The Bartered Bride
influence_en: He laid the foundations of Czech national music, and his achievement was carried to a world-class level by his junior Antonín Dvořák.

bio_en: A member of the Russian "Five". His main profession was as a chemist and physician, and he composed in his spare time as a "Sunday composer". He is famous for the "Polovtsian Dances" from the opera Prince Igor and the symphonic poem In the Steppes of Central Asia.
style_en: Russian Five, nationalist school, epic and exotic melodies, the opera Prince Igor (Polovtsian Dances)
influence_en: His exotic, vigorous melodies became one of the hallmarks of Russian music, and his melodies were later used in the musical Kismet.

bio_en: French composer, pianist and organist. So versatile that he was called the "Mendelssohn of France", he valued Classical formal beauty. He left many famous works, including The Carnival of the Animals, Danse macabre and the Symphony No. 3, the "Organ" Symphony.
style_en: Classical Romanticism, eclecticism, The Carnival of the Animals, Danse macabre, Symphony No. 3 "Organ"
influence_en: He founded the Société Nationale de Musique, contributed to the revival of French instrumental music, and influenced younger composers such as Fauré and Ravel.

bio_en: German late Romantic composer. He was a conservative composer who followed the tradition of Mendelssohn and Brahms. His Violin Concerto No. 1 in G minor remains one of the finest Romantic violin concertos and brought him immortal fame.
style_en: late Romanticism, Violin Concerto No. 1, Scottish Fantasy, Kol Nidrei for cello
influence_en: His Violin Concerto No. 1, together with the concertos of Mendelssohn and Brahms, is firmly established in the standard repertoire of violinists.

bio_en: The most successful French opera composer of the late 19th century. Following Gounod, he reigned as the master of French lyric opera. He is best known for the "Méditation" from the opera Thaïs and for the opera Manon.
style_en: French lyric opera (drame lyrique), Méditation from Thaïs, Manon, sweet and graceful melodies
influence_en: His operatic style also influenced Puccini, and as a professor at the Paris Conservatoire he taught many pupils.

bio_en: Spanish violin virtuoso and composer. He was one of the finest virtuoso violinists of the late 19th century, following Paganini. To show off his technique he composed many brilliant works in Spanish folk style, of which Zigeunerweisen is the most famous.
style_en: violin virtuoso, Zigeunerweisen, Carmen Fantasy, Spanish folk style, brilliant technique
influence_en: His playing and works form an important part of the violin repertoire. Lalo, Bruch, Saint-Saëns and others dedicated works to him.

bio_en: English composer. He ended the dark age of English music that had lasted two hundred years since Purcell's death and led a revival of English music. He is famous for the Enigma Variations, the Cello Concerto and the Pomp and Circumstance March No. 1 (called Britain's second national anthem).
style_en: English late Romanticism, Pomp and Circumstance, Enigma Variations, Cello Concerto
influence_en: He established a distinct identity for English music and opened the way for younger English composers such as Vaughan Williams and Holst.

bio_en: Italian composer. With Mascagni he was a leading figure of "verismo" (realist) opera. His one-act opera Pagliacci, based on a real murder case, was a runaway hit and brought him immortal fame.
style_en: verismo (realist) opera, Pagliacci, "Vesti la giubba"
influence_en: Pagliacci, together with Mascagni's Cavalleria rusticana, is known by the shorthand "Cav and Pag" and is the most representative work of verismo opera, often performed together to this day.

bio_en: A composer and pianist representing the Spanish nationalist school. He splendidly transformed the folk rhythms of Spain's various regions and guitar techniques into piano music. The piano suite Iberia is considered his greatest masterpiece.
style_en: Spanish nationalist school, piano music, Iberia, Suite española (Asturias, Sevilla)
influence_en: Together with Granados and Falla, he laid the foundations of modern Spanish music, and his piano idiom also influenced the Impressionism of Debussy and Ravel.

bio_en: Italian composer. His one-act opera Cavalleria rusticana, composed at the age of 26, was an enormous success and opened the age of "verismo" (realist) opera. Its "Intermezzo" is very famous.
style_en: verismo (realist) opera, Cavalleria rusticana, intense and passionate drama
influence_en: His Cavalleria rusticana, together with Leoncavallo's Pagliacci, became the origin and representative work of verismo opera, and greatly influenced Puccini as well.

bio_en: A national hero of Finland and one of the greatest symphonists of the 20th century. He put into his music the spirit of Finland resisting Russian rule. He is famous for the symphonic poem Finlandia, Valse triste and the Violin Concerto in D minor.
style_en: Finnish nationalist school, the symphonic poem Finlandia, seven symphonies, Violin Concerto, the cold, majestic nature of the Nordic countries
influence_en: Through his music he inspired the Finnish people's longing for independence, and, together with Mahler and Nielsen, he is regarded as a master who carried on the tradition of the 20th-century symphony.

bio_en: A master who led English music of the 20th century after Elgar. He collected and studied English folk songs and Renaissance music and blended them into modern symphonies and orchestral works. Fantasia on Greensleeves is his most famous piece.
style_en: English nationalist school, English folk songs, nine symphonies, Fantasia on Greensleeves, The Lark Ascending
influence_en: Together with Holst, he established a distinct identity for English music, and his music had a deep influence on English composers of the 20th century.

bio_en: English composer. His orchestral suite The Planets, depicting seven planets, has gained worldwide popularity. The fourth movement, "Jupiter", is especially famous. He was also deeply drawn to Hindu philosophy.
style_en: the orchestral suite The Planets, English folk songs, Hindu philosophy, distinctive orchestration
influence_en: His Planets suite is counted among the masterpieces of 20th-century orchestral music, and the "Mars" movement in particular had a great influence on later film music, such as John Williams's Star Wars score.

bio_en: German composer and pianist. Today he is known only for his 25 Études, Op. 100, for beginning pianists. This collection of études, which carries Romantic lyricism, has become an essential textbook for piano students around the world.
style_en: études for piano teaching, 25 Études, Op. 100
influence_en: Together with Czerny's, his études are among the most basic repertoire of piano teaching and have contributed to the introductory training of countless pianists.

bio_en: Russian pianist and composer. In his day he was the finest pianist, rivaling Liszt, but he did not achieve great success as a composer. He founded the St. Petersburg Conservatory (1862), Russia's first conservatory, and laid the foundations of Russian music education.
style_en: Western European-style Romanticism, pianist, Melody in F major
influence_en: The conservatory he founded produced many musicians, including Tchaikovsky, and established an academic Russian musical tradition distinct from the nationalist school of the "Five".

bio_en: Violin virtuoso and composer of Polish origin. Together with Sarasate, he was a leading violinist of the late 19th century. His Violin Concerto No. 2 in D minor and Polonaise brillante are important repertoire for violinists.
style_en: violin virtuoso, Violin Concerto No. 2, polonaise, Polish folk style
influence_en: His works combined violin virtuosity with lyricism, carrying on to some extent on the violin what Chopin had achieved on the piano.

bio_en: Spanish guitarist and composer, called the "father of the modern classical guitar". He systematized guitar technique and, by arranging works by Bach, Chopin and others for the guitar, raised it to the status of a concert instrument. Recuerdos de la Alhambra is his most famous piece.
style_en: father of the modern classical guitar, Recuerdos de la Alhambra, tremolo technique, guitar transcriptions
influence_en: His teaching method, works and arrangements were passed on to later guitarists such as Andrés Segovia and became the foundation of the classical guitar today.

bio_en: Austrian composer. Following Schubert, Schumann and Brahms, he was the finest composer of the German Lied in the late 19th century. Influenced by Wagner, he combined poetry and music dramatically, and left song collections devoted to the poems of single poets (Goethe, Mörike and others).
style_en: master of the German Lied, influence of Wagner (chromaticism), dramatic union of poetry and music, the "Mörike Lieder"
influence_en: He brought the German Lied to the last peak of Romanticism, and together with Richard Strauss he is regarded as one of the two pillars of the late Romantic song.

bio_en: The greatest composer Denmark produced and a national hero. Together with Sibelius he is a symphonist representing 20th-century Nordic music. He composed six symphonies, and the Symphony No. 4, "The Inextinguishable", is especially famous.
style_en: Danish nationalist school, six symphonies, "progressive tonality"
influence_en: While carrying on the Brahms tradition, he built a symphonic world of his own and raised Danish music to a world-class level.

bio_en: A composer representing late Russian Romanticism. A pupil of Rimsky-Korsakov, he blended the nationalist school of the "Five" with Tchaikovsky's Western European style. He is famous for the ballet Raymonda and the Violin Concerto in A minor. He served for many years as director of the St. Petersburg Conservatory.
style_en: late Russian Romanticism, the ballet Raymonda, Violin Concerto, master of orchestration
influence_en: He taught many pupils, including Shostakovich, and is regarded as the composer who brilliantly capped Russian Romanticism.

bio_en: German late Romantic composer. Inheriting the Brahms tradition, he devoted himself to reviving the complex counterpoint and fugal technique of J.S. Bach. He left unrivaled achievements especially in works for the organ.
style_en: late Romanticism, revival of Bach's counterpoint, fugue, organ music, absolute music
influence_en: His complex harmony and counterpoint influenced Schoenberg and the "Second Viennese School", serving as a bridge from Romanticism to 20th-century modernism.

bio_en: The finest Spanish composer of the 20th century, following Albéniz and Granados. He combined Spanish folk music (especially Andalusian flamenco) with modern techniques such as Impressionism and neoclassicism. He is famous for the ballets El amor brujo and The Three-Cornered Hat.
style_en: Spanish nationalist school, Andalusian flamenco (cante jondo), Impressionism, El amor brujo
influence_en: He led Spanish music into the mainstream of 20th-century modern music, and his music is said to express the distinctive feeling of Spain in its most refined form.

bio_en: One of the greatest masters, with the greatest influence on 20th-century music. He changed his style sharply from period to period (primitivism, neoclassicism, serialism), so much so that he was called a "chameleon". The three early ballets he composed for the Ballets Russes, The Firebird, Petrushka and The Rite of Spring, revolutionized music history.
style_en: primitivist rhythms, polytonality, irregular meters, neoclassicism, serialism, The Rite of Spring
influence_en: The Rite of Spring, premiered in Paris in 1913, caused a scandal with its dissonance and primitive rhythms and announced the real beginning of 20th-century music. Together with Schoenberg, he is regarded as one of the two great figures who set the direction of 20th-century music.

bio_en: The greatest revolutionary of 20th-century music. In his early years he wrote late Romantic music such as Verklärte Nacht, but he gradually experimented with "atonality", which destroys tonality, and finally created the "twelve-tone technique" (dodecaphony), which uses all twelve notes equally. He fled the Nazis and emigrated to the United States.
style_en: late Romanticism, Expressionism, atonality, twelve-tone technique (serialism), Second Viennese School
influence_en: His twelve-tone technique was a revolution that fundamentally undermined the tonal system of Western music that had lasted for several hundred years. With his pupils Alban Berg and Anton Webern he formed the "Second Viennese School", and his ideas had an absolute influence on composers all over the world after World War II.

bio_en: The finest symphonist and string quartet composer of the 20th century. Under the repression of the Soviet system, sometimes conforming to it (Symphony No. 5) and sometimes resisting, he left fifteen symphonies and fifteen string quartets. His music is regarded as an art that bears witness to the anguish of 20th-century humanity and to its era.
style_en: 20th-century neoclassicism, influence of Mahler, intense dynamics, satire and the grotesque, tragic quality, the DSCH motif (a signature drawn from his own initials)
influence_en: He is the last great master to carry the symphonic tradition running from Beethoven to Mahler into the 20th century. His works are among the most frequently performed of the 20th-century repertoire today, and continue to influence contemporary composers deeply.

bio_en: Together with Stravinsky and Shostakovich, one of the three great masters representing 20th-century Russia. After the Revolution he worked in the West before returning to the Soviet Union. He left many popular works, including the ballet Romeo and Juliet, the musical fairy tale Peter and the Wolf, and the Symphony No. 1, the "Classical Symphony".
style_en: neoclassicism, sharp rhythms, motoric rhythms, rich lyricism, the grotesque and wit (sarcasm)
influence_en: As a leading figure of 20th-century neoclassicism, he combined Classical formal beauty with modern harmony. His ballet music and piano sonatas are firmly established in the standard 20th-century repertoire.

bio_en: Great Hungarian composer, pianist and ethnomusicologist. Together with Kodály, he collected and analyzed Hungarian and Eastern European folk songs and combined them perfectly with his own modern compositional techniques. Concerto for Orchestra and Music for Strings, Percussion and Celesta are counted as his masterpieces.
style_en: nationalism, Eastern European folk songs, irregular rhythms, the golden section, counterpoint, Mikrokosmos (a collection of piano studies)
influence_en: He was a pioneer of ethnomusicology. He made a profound contribution to 20th-century music by elevating folk song from mere quotation into a central idiom of modern music.

bio_en: A composer who is a symbol of American music. He was the first to successfully combine classical (symphonic) music with jazz. He left immortal hits such as Rhapsody in Blue, An American in Paris and the opera Porgy and Bess.
style_en: symphonic jazz, Rhapsody in Blue, fusion of jazz and the blues, Broadway musicals, the opera Porgy and Bess
influence_en: He was a pioneer who gave birth to a distinctly American art music. He influenced European composers such as Ravel, and by breaking down the boundary between classical and popular music he opened the way for later composers such as Leonard Bernstein.

bio_en: The "Renaissance man" representing America in the late 20th century. He was a world-famous conductor, composer, pianist and music educator (Young People's Concerts). With the musical West Side Story he broke down the boundary between Broadway and classical music.
style_en: the musical West Side Story, fusion of classical, jazz and Latin music, symphonies, passionate conducting, music education
influence_en: With West Side Story he raised the musical to a symphonic, operatic level. As a conductor and educator he also revived the music of Mahler and contributed greatly to popularizing classical music.

bio_en: Korean composer and conductor. He is the composer of South Korea's national anthem, "Aegukga". He studied with Kodály in Hungary and with Richard Strauss in Austria. He composed the symphonic poem Korea Fantasy, based on his own Aegukga theme.
style_en: late Romantic orchestration, the symphonic poem Korea Fantasy, Aegukga
influence_en: By composing "Aegukga" he has had an absolute influence on every Korean. Korea Fantasy has historical significance as an early example of expressing Korean material through Western late Romantic orchestral music. (He has a record of conducting the Berlin Philharmonic, and there is controversy over his pro-Japanese and pro-Nazi associations.)

bio_en: Korea's first full-fledged Western-style musician: composer, violinist, conductor and critic. He gave Korea's first violin recital, and by composing the first Korean art song (gagok), Bongseonhwa, and the beloved children's song Spring in My Hometown (Gohyang-ui Bom), he laid the foundations of Western music in Korea.
style_en: pioneer of the Korean art song, Bongseonhwa, Spring in My Hometown, 7-5 syllable meter, lyricism, the violin piece Melody of Sorrow
influence_en: By pioneering Korean art songs and children's songs that carry the feeling of the Korean people, he played a decisive role in Western music taking root in Korea. (There is controversy over his pro-Japanese activities.)

bio_en: The most widely known Korean composer in the world. Based in Darmstadt, Germany, he combined Western avant-garde techniques (twelve-tone) with Eastern thought (Taoism, yin-yang) and Korean traditional music techniques (nonghyeon, or vibrato, and sigimsae, or ornamentation) in an original way. He suffered ordeals in 1967 in the "East Berlin Affair".
style_en: fusion of Eastern thought and Western avant-garde, twelve-tone technique, the "Hauptton" (main tone) technique, transfer of Korean traditional music techniques (sigimsae, nonghyeon) to Western instruments, the opera Sim Tjong
influence_en: By presenting Eastern philosophy and sound in an original way to the Western musical world, he was highly regarded as a "mediator between East and West". He is the only East Asian composer to have left a distinct mark on 20th-century Western music history.

bio_en: German composer. The stage cantata Carmina Burana, based on medieval poetry, brought him immortal fame. One of its pieces, "O Fortuna", is overwhelmingly used in films, advertising and popular media and has become one of the most famous pieces in classical music history.
style_en: Carmina Burana (O Fortuna), primitivism, intense and repetitive rhythms, simple harmony, the "Orff Schulwerk" (music education method)
influence_en: His music education method (Schulwerk), centered on rhythm instruments, had a great influence on 20th-century music education. Carmina Burana is the most popularly successful of all 20th-century works.

bio_en: The most revolutionary American composer and thinker of the 20th century. He posed the fundamental question "What is music?" He experimented with 4′33″, in which the performer plays nothing, "chance music" and the "prepared piano".
style_en: chance music (aleatoric music), indeterminacy, 4′33″, prepared piano, electronic music, Zen thought
influence_en: By asking "Can noise be music?", he had an absolute influence on the late 20th-century avant-garde, performance art (Fluxus) and minimalism. He was also a great inspiration to the artistic activity of Nam June Paik.

bio_en: American composer. Together with Steve Reich, he is one of the best-known living composers, a founder and popularizer of "minimalist" music. He is also famous for the opera Einstein on the Beach and for the scores of the films The Hours and The Truman Show.
style_en: minimalism, repeating arpeggios, gradual change of simple harmony, film music
influence_en: He brought minimalism to a popular genre, and his addictive style has been widely absorbed into contemporary film music, pop and ambient music.

bio_en: The finest composer to revive English music in the 20th century since Purcell. He left a masterpiece of educational music in The Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra, and also top masterpieces of 20th-century opera and sacred music, such as the opera Peter Grimes and the War Requiem.
style_en: neoclassicism, English lyricism, the opera Peter Grimes, The Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra, War Requiem
influence_en: Following Elgar, he established the identity of English music in the 20th century, and his operas in particular, together with Stravinsky's The Rake's Progress, are regarded as the summit of 20th-century neoclassical opera.

bio_en: The most original master of 20th-century French music. By combining disparate elements such as devout Catholic faith, the transcription of birdsong and Indian rhythms (tala), he built a mystical musical world of his own. He is famous for the Quatuor pour la fin du temps (Quartet for the End of Time), composed in a prisoner-of-war camp in World War II.
style_en: transcription of birdsong, mysticism, Indian rhythms (tala), modes of limited transposition, pioneer of total serialism, organ music
influence_en: His compositional method and harmony (the Messiaen modes) had a decisive influence on the post-World War II generation of "total serialism", including Pierre Boulez and Stockhausen.

bio_en: A pupil of Schoenberg and, with Webern, a core member of the "Second Viennese School". He successfully combined his teacher's innovative twelve-tone technique with the late Romantic lyricism of Gustav Mahler. His operas Wozzeck and Lulu and his Violin Concerto are counted among his masterpieces.
style_en: Second Viennese School, combination of twelve-tone technique and Romanticism, the Expressionist opera Wozzeck, Violin Concerto "To the Memory of an Angel"
influence_en: He proved that rich emotional expression and dramatic power are possible even within the strict framework of twelve-tone technique, and served as the most important bridge connecting atonal music to the general public.

bio_en: A pupil of Schoenberg (Second Viennese School). He pushed his teacher's twelve-tone technique to the furthest extreme, pursuing an extremely compressed and restrained formal beauty. His music is likened to "pointillism", and a single piece is often only one or two minutes long.
style_en: Second Viennese School, extreme brevity (aphorism), pointillism, structuring of the tone row, forerunner of "total serialism"
influence_en: His music was hardly performed in his lifetime, but after World War II it became an absolute textbook for postwar avant-garde composers such as Stockhausen and Boulez, opening the age of "total serialism".

bio_en: The "father of American modern music". His main profession was as an insurance man, and he composed independently. He discovered, on his own or even earlier, the innovative techniques of 20th-century Europe, such as polytonality, atonality, complex rhythm and collage. The Unanswered Question and the Concord Sonata are famous.
style_en: polytonality, atonality, complex rhythm, quotation of American folk songs and hymns (collage), The Unanswered Question
influence_en: Almost unknown in his lifetime, he was reappraised after his death and is revered as a pioneer who symbolizes a distinctly American spirit of experimentation, unbound by the European tradition.

bio_en: Argentine bandoneon player and composer. He created "Nuevo Tango" (new tango), which combines traditional tango with classical music (fugue, counterpoint) and jazz (improvisation), and raised tango to the level of art. Libertango and Adiós Nonino are famous.
style_en: nuevo tango, bandoneon, Libertango, Adiós Nonino, Oblivion, fusion of tango, classical and jazz
influence_en: He elevated tango from dance music to "music for listening". His music crosses the boundary between classical and popular music and is loved around the world, and it is reinterpreted by countless classical performers.

bio_en: French composer. He is known for simple, meditative piano pieces such as the Gymnopédies and Gnossiennes. Rejecting the grandeur and seriousness of Romanticism, he was an eccentric pioneer who advocated "furniture music" as "background music".
style_en: Gymnopédies, Gnossiennes, simplicity, repetition, forerunner of minimalism, "furniture music" (Musique d'ameublement), anti-Romanticism, Surrealism
influence_en: His simple, rebellious attitude directly influenced Debussy, Ravel and the French Six (Poulenc, Milhaud), and in the late 20th century he was reappraised as a precursor of John Cage and minimalist music.

bio_en: A composer representing Soviet Armenia. The "Sabre Dance" from the ballet Gayane became a worldwide sensation. The Adagio from the ballet Spartacus is also famous. Together with Shostakovich and Prokofiev he represented the Soviet Union.
style_en: the "Sabre Dance" from the ballet Gayane, the ballet Spartacus, Armenian folk music, intense rhythms, exotic melodies
influence_en: He introduced Armenian folk music to the world by combining it with Western orchestral writing, and his "Sabre Dance" became one of the most famous hits of 20th-century classical music.

bio_en: A world-renowned artist produced by Korea, the "founder of video art". He studied music and aesthetics in Tokyo and Germany and, influenced by John Cage, worked in avant-garde and performance art (Fluxus) groups, presenting performances such as "smashing a violin".
style_en: video art, Fluxus, performance art, "TV Cello", "The More, the Better", avant-garde music
influence_en: Rather than as a composer, he made his mark on 20th-century art history as a visual artist and performance artist. His ideas combining music, technology and performance had a profound influence on contemporary media art.

bio_en: A first-generation composer counted, with Hong Nan-pa, as one of the two great pillars of Korean art song. He composed songs with bold, lyrical melodies, such as Gagopa (Longing to Go), Mongnyeonhwa (Magnolia) and Nae maeumeun (My Heart). He also composed the opera Simcheongjeon (The Tale of Sim Cheong).
style_en: Korean art song, Romantic lyricism, Gagopa, Mongnyeonhwa, Nae maeumeun, the opera Simcheongjeon
influence_en: Through songs that best express the feeling of the Korean people, he is a master who raised the standard of Korean art song a level higher. (There is controversy over pro-Japanese ties related to Manchukuo.)

bio_en: The finest Czech nationalist composer of the 20th century, following Dvořák. He studied the folk songs of Moravia in the Czech lands and the intonation of the language ("speech melody") and wrote original operas (Jenůfa, The Cunning Little Vixen) and instrumental works (Sinfonietta).
style_en: Czech nationalist school, the "speech melody" theory, intense realism, the opera Jenůfa, Sinfonietta
influence_en: One of the most original opera composers of the 20th century, he is being reappraised, together with Bartók, as a pioneer in the modern use of folk song.

bio_en: The greatest composer of 20th-century South America, representing Brazil. He is famous for the cycle of nine Bachianas Brasileiras, which combine Brazilian folk music with the counterpoint of J.S. Bach.
style_en: Bachianas Brasileiras, Brazilian folk music, neoclassicism, guitar études
influence_en: He established an art music that carries Brazil's own identity, leaving a major mark on 20th-century nationalist music. Bachianas Brasileiras No. 5 (for soprano and cello ensemble) is especially famous.

bio_en: A leading German composer, violist and theorist of the 20th century. He fled to the United States to escape the Nazi suppression of "degenerate music". He advocated "utility music" (Gebrauchsmusik) for amateur performers and is an important figure of 20th-century neoclassicism.
style_en: neoclassicism, "utility music" (Gebrauchsmusik), New Objectivity (Neue Sachlichkeit), extended tonal system, the opera Mathis der Maler
influence_en: His compositional theory had a great influence on 20th-century composition teaching, and he is regarded as a composer representing 20th-century neoclassicism.

bio_en: A member of the French Les Six of the 20th century. Influenced by Erik Satie, he composed music that is witty and refined and at the same time deeply religious and lyrical. His songs (mélodies) and the opera Dialogues of the Carmelites are famous.
style_en: Les Six, neoclassicism, French song (mélodie), wit and lyricism, sacred music (Gloria), the opera Dialogues of the Carmelites
influence_en: A leading figure of 20th-century French music in the line of Satie and Debussy. His roughly 200 songs and his sacred choral music in particular are counted among the finest masterpieces of the 20th century.

bio_en: A leader of the "avant-garde" of the late 20th century after World War II. He was a pioneer of "total serialism", "electronic music" and "spatial music", developing the ideas of Webern. He also caused controversy by calling the September 11 attacks "the greatest work of art".
style_en: total serialism, electronic music (Elektronische Musik), chance music, spatial music, Gesang der Jünglinge (Song of the Youths)
influence_en: Together with Pierre Boulez and Luigi Nono, he led the direction of late 20th-century music, centered on Darmstadt, and his experiments also influenced popular music such as the Beatles.

bio_en: Italian master who, with Stockhausen and Boulez, led the avant-garde of the late 20th century. He is famous for Sinfonia, which quotes Mahler's symphony, and for the Sequenza cycle, which explores the technique of various instruments.
style_en: avant-garde, electronic music, collage technique, Sinfonia, Sequenza
influence_en: He contributed greatly to expanding the musical language of the late 20th century, and the Sequenza cycle in particular became a textbook of 20th-century instrumental technique.

bio_en: A master composer representing 20th-century Poland. Influenced by Chopin and Bartók, and by John Cage, he built a sound world of his own, using techniques such as "limited aleatory". The Concerto for Orchestra is famous.
style_en: avant-garde, "limited aleatory" (aleatoric counterpoint), Concerto for Orchestra, symphonies
influence_en: Together with Penderecki he led the revival of 20th-century Polish music and is regarded as a leading figure of the Eastern European avant-garde.

bio_en: One of the greatest film composers of the 20th century. He scored all of Federico Fellini's films, and won immortal fame with the music for Francis Ford Coppola's Godfather trilogy. "A Time for Us" from Romeo and Juliet (1968) is also his work.
style_en: film music: The Godfather, Romeo and Juliet (1968), La Strada, lyrical and sweet melodies
influence_en: His film music goes beyond mere background music to an art that governs the emotion of a film, and made a profound contribution to 20th-century film history.

bio_en: American film composer. He made his debut with Citizen Kane and is especially famous for his collaborations with Alfred Hitchcock (Psycho, Vertigo, North by Northwest). Taxi Driver was his last work.
style_en: film music: Psycho (strings only), Vertigo, dissonance, suspense, ostinato (repeated phrase)
influence_en: The sharp string sound of Psycho was a revolution in film music and created the archetype of sound expressing suspense and horror.

bio_en: A first-generation Korean contemporary composer who followed Isang Yun. He was the first Korean to take part in the Darmstadt contemporary music festival, and in 1966 he presented Korea's first electronic music, Feast of Primary Colors (Wonsaek-ui Hyangyeon). He taught at Seoul National University and trained many pupils.
style_en: Korea's first-generation avant-garde, Korea's first electronic music, fusion of East and West
influence_en: By introducing and teaching 20th-century Western avant-garde techniques in earnest in Korea, and training younger composers such as Unsuk Chin, he served as a godfather of Korean contemporary music.

bio_en: A first-generation Korean composer. Called a "prolific composer", he left a vast body of some 4,000 works, including the songs Dalbam (Moonlit Night) and Yeohowaneun naui mokjasi-ni (The Lord Is My Shepherd). He mastered every genre: church music, songs, symphonies and operas.
style_en: Korean Romanticism, church music (hymns), the song Dalbam (Moonlit Night), use of Korean scales
influence_en: Through his vast output and teaching, he left a major mark on the development of Korean music in the 20th century.

bio_en: A first-generation composer and pianist who, together with Hong Nan-pa and Kim Dong-jin, laid the cornerstone of Korean art song. He left gem-like art songs and children's songs such as Seomjip Agi (The Island Baby), Bawigogae (Rocky Pass) and Eomeoni-ui Maeum (A Mother's Heart).
style_en: Korean art song, children's songs, Seomjip Agi, Bawigogae, lyricism
influence_en: His works, such as Seomjip Agi and A Mother's Heart, have become songs beloved across generations by all Koreans, sung as national favorites.

bio_en: A first-generation Korean composer. He is famous for songs that evoke nostalgia and sorrow, such as Seonguja (The Pioneer) and Geurium (Longing). Because of his record of working as a "Manchukuo composer", he is the subject of pro-Japanese controversy.
style_en: Korean art song, Seonguja, continental romanticism, sorrow
