influence_en: Seonguja was widely sung in the 1970s and 80s, but today opinion is divided because of historical controversy, and the song has even been removed from textbooks.

bio_en: Norwegian composer and pianist. After studying at the Leipzig Conservatory, he worked the melodies and rhythms of Norwegian folk songs and dance music into his works and became the composer representing the Norwegian nationalist school. He is famous for the Piano Concerto in A minor, the incidental music for Ibsen's play Peer Gynt, and the 66 Lyric Pieces.
style_en: Norwegian folk melodies and dance rhythms (halling, springar), lyrical piano miniatures, delicate harmony, Peer Gynt, Piano Concerto in A minor
influence_en: He added the color of Norwegian folk music to the idiom of German Romanticism and opened the way for the Nordic nationalist school. His harmony also influenced French composers such as Debussy and Ravel.

bio_en: German composer and conductor. He is counted as the last great master of German late Romanticism, following Liszt and Wagner. In his youth he made his name with symphonic poems such as Don Juan and Also sprach Zarathustra, and in the 20th century he had great success with operas such as Salome, Elektra and Der Rosenkavalier.
style_en: symphonic poems, brilliant orchestration for vast forces, leitmotif, bold dissonance (Salome, Elektra), lyrical melodies for soprano
influence_en: He raised the symphonic poem that Liszt began to the peak of orchestral description, and carried on the lineage of German opera after Wagner until the mid-20th century. The opening of Also sprach Zarathustra was used in the film 2001: A Space Odyssey and became widely known to the general public.

bio_en: Hungarian-born Austrian composer. Born into a Hungarian-Jewish family in Transylvania, Romania, he fled to Vienna just after the Hungarian Revolution of 1956. He wrote pieces such as Atmosphères and Lux aeterna from tightly layered textures of many voices, and when these were used in the film 2001: A Space Odyssey they became known to the general public.
style_en: micropolyphony, sound masses, complex polyrhythm, machine-like rhythm, piano études
influence_en: He opened the way to weaving music from changes of timbre and texture instead of melody and harmony, becoming a composer representing the late 20th-century avant-garde. From 1973 to 1989 he taught composition at the Hamburg University of Music, and among his pupils was Unsuk Chin.

bio_en: American composer. He studied at the Curtis Institute and is regarded as a composer who preserved Romantic lyricism and traditional harmony rather than the experiments of 20th-century modernism. His best-known work is the Adagio for Strings, premiered by Toscanini in 1938, and he won the Pulitzer Prize twice, for the opera Vanessa and for a piano concerto.
style_en: neo-Romanticism, long-breathed lyrical melodies, traditional tonality and form, songs and choral music, Adagio for Strings
influence_en: The Adagio for Strings has become America's representative memorial music, used in broadcasts after the news of President Roosevelt's death and after the funeral of President Kennedy. It was also used in the films The Elephant Man and Platoon, becoming widely known.

bio_en: French composer, critic and teacher. He was so strict with himself that he destroyed works he was not satisfied with, so not many pieces survive. His best-known work is the symphonic scherzo The Sorcerer's Apprentice, based on a poem by Goethe, which became better known after being used in Disney's film Fantasia.
style_en: meticulous form and construction, brilliant orchestration, influence of Franck and d'Indy, Impressionist color, the symphonic scherzo The Sorcerer's Apprentice
influence_en: He taught composition at the Paris Conservatoire and the École Normale, training Messiaen, Duruflé, Rodrigo and others. In the French musical world of his day, split between conservatives and progressives, he took neither side and was respected by both.

bio_en: Italian composer, violinist and musicologist. In 1900 he worked as principal violist of the Imperial Theatre orchestra in St. Petersburg, where he studied orchestration with Rimsky-Korsakov. From 1913 he taught composition in Rome, and he gained international fame with the "Roman Trilogy": Fountains of Rome, Pines of Rome and Roman Festivals.
style_en: brilliant, colorful orchestration, the Roman Trilogy of symphonic poems, borrowing from Gregorian chant and old Italian music, pictorial description
influence_en: In an Italian musical world centered on opera, he was a rare composer who achieved international success with orchestral works. He also worked to revive old Italian music, as in Ancient Airs and Dances, which transcribes Renaissance lute music for orchestra.

bio_en: Violinist and composer from Vienna, Austria. With his sweet tone and expression that made use of portamento and rubato, he was a leading violinist of the first half of the 20th century, and in 1910 he premiered Elgar's Violin Concerto. He left pieces with a Viennese feeling, such as Liebesfreud (Love's Joy), Liebesleid (Love's Sorrow) and Schön Rosmarin.
style_en: Viennese-waltz-style violin miniatures, sweet tone, portamento and rubato, works borrowing the style of old masters, encore pieces
influence_en: His miniatures are still regular encores in violin recitals, and the cadenzas he wrote for Beethoven's Violin Concerto are the most often played today. In 1935 he revealed that several works he had presented as pieces by older masters such as Pugnani and Tartini were in fact his own.
